summary: Stops the user to confirm an action with consequences, usually destructive: delete tokens, revoke access, force publish. It asks one question and offers two answers.
whenToUse: Before an action that cannot be undone or that affects other people: deleting, revoking, overwriting.
tone primary for consequential but safe actions, like publishing a release to every consumer.
whenNotToUse: Actions that can be undone: do them right away and offer Undo in a Toast.
Routine saves: confirmation fatigue teaches people to click through without reading.

dos.title: Ask a question that names the action and the object
dos.text: "Delete 3 tokens?" with a confirm button "Delete tokens" is understood without reading the description.

dos.title: Say the consequence, including what cannot be undone
dos.text: "Components that use them fall back to their defaults. This cannot be undone."

donts.title: "Are you sure?" with Yes and No
donts.text: It hides what is about to happen. Name the action in the title and on the button.

accessibility: Base UI AlertDialog: role alertdialog, named by the title, described by the consequence.
Focus starts on Cancel, the safe choice, so a reflexive Enter does not destroy anything.
It does not close on an outside click; Escape and Cancel close it and focus returns to the trigger.
While loading, the confirm button keeps focus and announces aria-busy.
contentGuidelines: Title: a question with the verb and the object and a count when there are several: "Delete 3 tokens?"
Description: the consequence in one or two sentences. End with "This cannot be undone." only when true.
Confirm label repeats the verb: "Delete tokens", "Revoke access". Never "OK" or "Yes".
